artworks.title: The Birth of Venus
artworks.description: Botticelli's Uffizi masterpiece: Zephyrus, locked with the breeze-nymph Aura, blows Venus ashore on her shell — the west wind as Renaissance art's most famous breath of spring.

artworks.title: Primavera
artworks.description: On the left edge of Botticelli's Primavera, Zephyrus seizes the nymph Chloris, who transforms into Flora — the west wind as the violent spark that turns the orchard into spring.

artworks.title: Flora and Zephyr
artworks.description: Bouguereau's Mulhouse canvas: Zephyr, winged and airborne, lifts Flora among putti and roses — academic polish on the Ovidian marriage of west wind and flowers.

artworks.title: Flora Caressed by Zephyr
artworks.description: Gérard's Grenoble painting: Zephyr leans from the air to kiss Flora — Neoclassical tenderness for the breeze that brings the year's first blossoms.

popCulture.title: The Birth of Venus
popCulture.creator: Sandro Botticelli
popCulture.description: Botticelli's Zephyrus blows Venus ashore on her shell — the west wind as Renaissance art's most famous breath of spring.

popCulture.title: Zephyr
popCulture.description: English zephyr names a soft breeze — Zephyrus reduced to the everyday word for gentle western air.
